q: Why does a cache hold 220 RPS against a 200 RPS origin?
a: Repeat keys hit the edge in ~2ms, so the origin only serves misses and stays under capacity.

q: What happens when TTL drops below the key revisit cycle?
a: Entries expire before repeats arrive, nearly every request misses, and the shield collapses to direct-origin numbers.
A cold or expired cache sends a miss storm at the origin at once, queueing it past SLO.

q: Why ask what cold looks like?
a: Every cache starts empty, so the opening miss burst must fit the origin buffer or the deploy itself causes the outage.
